# Spark UI (@sparkwire)

> React component library with a "Live Wire" look: components carry current (sparks on press, flowing current on hover, a lever switch with a bulb). Accessible behaviour from React Aria, zero-runtime CSS with --spark-* variables, light/dark/system modes, works in React Server Components. Use it as an npm package (@sparkwire/core) or copy the source (npx sparkwire add <name>).

Key facts for writing code:
- Import the stylesheet once: import '@sparkwire/core/styles.css'. Set the mode with data-spark-theme="dark" | "light" | "system" on <html> or any wrapper.
- App-wide defaults and slot classes: <SparkProvider components={{ Button: { defaultProps: { variant: 'outlined' } } }} locale="hi-IN">.
- Every component takes className, and most take classNames for inner parts. State is exposed as data-* attributes (data-state, data-open, data-invalid, data-disabled) for CSS or Tailwind.
- Forms: inputs take name and work with FormData and React Hook Form. Dropdown/Combobox/Slider/DatePicker submit through hidden inputs.
- Dates are plain JS Date objects; DatePicker submits ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Locales and calendar systems (indian, islamic-umalqura, buddhist...) are supported.
- Pick a value: Dropdown (alias Select). Search then pick: Combobox. Run actions: Menu.
- Custom markup with Spark behaviour: useSwitch, useCheckbox, useSlider, useDatePicker, useSpark from '@sparkwire/core/headless'. Building blocks: ButtonBase, InputBase, Popover, ListBox, Overlay from '@sparkwire/core/base'.
- The npm scope is @sparkwire (not @spark-ui, which is a different library).

## Button (`button`)
Throws sparks from the press point; current runs along outlined buttons on hover.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add button` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/actions-button--docs

### Button
Button: throws sparks from the press point. Outlined and text buttons show
current flowing along a wire on hover; a disabled button is a dead circuit.
Built on ButtonBase; forwards `ref` to the rendered element.

- `as?`: `ElementType` Render as another element or component, e.g. `"a"` or a router Link.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "icon", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, icon.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Dead circuit: no clicks, no sparks, dashed outline.
- `endIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon after the label. Coloured with the text.
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean` Stretch to the container's width.
- `spark?`: `boolean` Throw sparks from the press point on click. Default `true`.
- `startIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon before the label. Coloured with the text.
- `ripple?`: `boolean` **Deprecated.** Use `spark`. Kept so existing code keeps working.

## Spark (`spark`)
A burst of sparks from a point; used by Button and Calendar.

```tsx
import { Spark } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add spark` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/effects-spark--docs

### Spark
Spark: the signature Live Wire effect. Place it inside a `position: relative`
element and call `burst()` from its click handler. Renders nothing for users
who prefer reduced motion.

- `colors?`: `string[]` Particle colours. Defaults to the theme's `--spark-energy-spark-1…3`.
- `count?`: `number` (default `10`) Particles per burst. Default 10.
- `duration?`: `number` (default `700`) Burst duration in milliseconds. Default 700.
- `spread?`: `number` (default `70`) How far particles travel, in px. Default 70.

## Switch (`switch`)
A lever switch that lights a bulb.

```tsx
import { Switch } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add switch` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-switch--docs

### Switch
Switch: a lever that closes a circuit. When on, current lights the wire and
the bulb; when off, the lever lifts and the circuit goes dark.

Style hooks: `.sp-switch`, `[data-state="on"|"off"]`, and the parts
`.sp-switch__node`, `__wire`, `__lever`, `__bulb`, `__label`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `checked?`: `boolean` Controlled state.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"label" | "root" | "control" | "node" | "wire" | "lever" | "bulb", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, control, node, wire, lever, bulb, label.
- `color?`: `Tone` Colour of the current when on. Default `brand`.
- `defaultChecked?`: `boolean` Initial state when uncontrolled.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label. Use `aria-label` instead when there is none.
- `name?`: `string` Form field name. When set, a hidden input submits `value` while the switch is on.
- `onChange?`: `((checked: boolean, event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement, MouseEvent>) => void)` Called with the new state when the user flips the switch.
- `showBulb?`: `boolean` Show the bulb that lights when the circuit is closed. Default `true`.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.
- `value?`: `string` Value submitted with `name` while on. Default `"on"`.
- `wrapperClassName?`: `string` Class for the outer wrapper (the button gets `className`).

## Checkbox (`checkbox`)
A checkbox that closes a circuit.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add checkbox` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-checkbox--docs

### Checkbox
Checkbox: a terminal. Checking it powers the terminal: it fills with current
and the tick is drawn in. Built on a native checkbox, so forms and keyboards work.

Style hooks: `.sp-checkbox`, `__box`, `__label`, `__helper`; the native input
drives `:checked`, `:indeterminate` and `:disabled`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"label" | "root" | "box" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, box, label, helper.
- `color?`: `Tone` Colour when checked. Default `brand`.
- `error?`: `boolean` Marks the checkbox invalid and colours it with the error tone.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help or error text under the label.
- `indeterminate?`: `boolean` Shows a dash: some, but not all, of a group is selected.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Text next to the box.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.

## RadioGroup (`radio-group`)
One live wire at a time.

```tsx
import { RadioGroup } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add radio-group` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-radiogroup--docs

### RadioGroup
RadioGroup: a selector switch. Every option is a contact; only the chosen one
carries current, so its core lights up. Native radios underneath, so arrow
keys and forms work as expected.

Style hooks: `.sp-radio-group`, `__option[data-checked]`, `__dot`, `__text`.

- `label`: `ReactNode` The group's legend. Required for accessibility.
- `options`: `RadioOption[]`
- `className?`: `string`
- `color?`: `Tone` Colour of the chosen contact. Default `brand`.
- `defaultValue?`: `string` Initial value when uncontrolled.
- `error?`: `boolean` Marks the group invalid.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help or error text under the group.
- `name?`: `string` Form field name. Generated when omitted.
- `onChange?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `value?`: `string` Controlled value.
- `variant?`: `"list" | "cards"` `list` stacks options; `cards` lays them out as selectable cards.

## Slider (`slider`)
A dimmer, with two-knob ranges.

```tsx
import { Slider } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add slider` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-slider--docs

### Slider
Slider: a dimmer. The wire is lit up to the knob, and the glow gets stronger
the higher you turn it. Pass a `[start, end]` value for a range: current
flows between two knobs. Behaviour comes from React Aria: arrows, Page
Up/Down, Home/End, dragging, clicking the track, right-to-left, and
localized numbers. Each knob holds a native range input, so forms and
React Hook Form's `register` work.

Style hooks: `.sp-slider[data-range][data-disabled]`, `__header`, `__value`,
`__track`, `__fill`, `__thumb[data-dragging][data-focus-visible]`.
Variables: `--sp-start`, `--sp-end` and `--sp-pct` (0–100).

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"value" | "label" | "root" | "header" | "track" | "fill" | "thumb", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, header, label, value, track, fill, thumb.
- `color?`: `Tone` Default `brand`.
- `defaultValue?`: `SliderValue` Initial value when uncontrolled. A `[start, end]` pair makes it a range. Defaults to `min`.
- `formatOptions?`: `NumberFormatOptions` Intl number options when `formatValue` isn't set, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' }`.
- `formatValue?`: `((value: number) => string)` Format each value for the label and for screen readers.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label, shown with the current value.
- `max?`: `number` Default 100.
- `min?`: `number` Default 0.
- `name?`: `string | [string, string]` Form field name. For a range, one name (sent twice) or `[startName, endName]`.
- `onChange?`: `((value: T) => void)` Called on every move with the new value (a number, or `[start, end]`).
- `onChangeEnd?`: `((value: T) => void)` Called once when the user lets go, e.g. to save or fetch.
- `ref?`: `Ref<HTMLInputElement>`
- `step?`: `number` Default 1.
- `thumbLabels?`: `[string, string]` Screen-reader names for the two knobs of a range. Default `['Minimum', 'Maximum']`.
- `value?`: `SliderValue` Controlled value: a number, or `[start, end]` for a range with two knobs.

## Textfield (`textfield`)
A field that charges as you type.

```tsx
import { Textfield } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add textfield` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-textfield--docs

### Textfield
Textfield: in Live Wire, a field can "charge up" as its value becomes valid.
Pass `charge` (0..1, or a function of the value) to show the meter.

Style hooks: `.sp-textfield` with `[data-focused]`, `[data-invalid]`,
`[data-charged]`, `[data-disabled]`; parts `__label`, `__control`, `__input`,
`__adornment`, `__meter`, `__helper`. Built on InputBase (`.sp-input-base`).

- `append?`: `ReactNode`
- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `cardDetection?`: `((value: string) => string)`
- `charge?`: `number | ((value: string) => number)` Live Wire charge meter. A number from 0 to 1, or a function that maps the current value to 0..1 (e.g. password strength). At 1 the field is fully charged and current runs along the meter.
- `chargeLabel?`: `((percent: number) => ReactNode)` Text announced next to the meter. Receives the charge as 0..100.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"label" | "root" | "control" | "input" | "adornment" | "meter" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, control, input, adornment, meter, helper.
- `containerStyle?`: `CSSProperties`
- `defaultValue?`: `string` Initial value when uncontrolled (no `value`). Works with React Hook Form's `register`.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `error?`: `boolean`
- `formatPhoneNumber?`: `((value: string) => string)`
- `helperText?`: `string`
- `inputSize?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"`
- `isCurrency?`: `boolean`
- `label?`: `string` Visible label, linked to the input.
- `onBlur?`: `((event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement, Element>) => void)`
- `onChange?`: `((event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void)`
- `onFocus?`: `((event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement, Element>) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`
- `prepend?`: `ReactNode`
- `type?`: `"hidden" | "color" | "button" | "checkbox" | "date" | "datetime-local" | "email" | "file" | "image" | "month" | "password" | "radio" | "range" | "reset" | "search" | "submit" | ... 8 more ...`
- `value?`: `string`
- `variant?`: `"outlined" | "filled" | "standard"`

## Field (`field`)
Label, help text and error wiring for any control.

```tsx
import { Field } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add field` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-field--docs

### Field
Field: label, help text and error for any control, wired for screen readers.
Use it to give your own inputs (a textarea, a third-party editor) the same
labelling and error handling as Spark UI's built-in fields.

Style hooks: `.sp-field[data-invalid][data-disabled]`, `__label`,
`__required`, `__description`, `__error`.

- `children`: `ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ((props: FieldControlProps) => ReactNode)` One element (ids and aria props are added to it), or a function that receives the props to spread: `{(p) => <textarea {...p} />}`.
- `label`: `ReactNode` Visible label, linked to the control.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "description" | "error", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, description, error.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the control.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `error?`: `ReactNode` Error message. Replaces the description and marks the control invalid.
- `id?`: `string` Control id. Generated when omitted.
- `required?`: `boolean` Adds a required marker and `required` on the control.

## NumberField (`number-field`)
Locale-formatted numbers (₹1,00,000, %, units) with steppers.

```tsx
import { NumberField } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add number-field` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-numberfield--docs

### NumberField
NumberField: a number input that formats as you'd write it in your
language (₹1,00,000 in India, $100,000 in the US, 15 %, 2.5 kg). Up/Down
and the − / + buttons step; Page Up/Down step by tens; Home/End jump to
min/max; values are clamped and snapped to `step` on blur. Built on React
Aria's number field and the InputBase base component.

Style hooks: `.sp-number-field[data-invalid][data-disabled]`, `__label`,
`__stepper`, `__helper`; the field is `.sp-input-base`.

- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "field" | "input" | "stepper" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, field, input, stepper, helper.
- `defaultValue?`: `number | null`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `error?`: `ReactNode` An error message, or `true` to mark the field invalid and show `helperText` as the error.
- `formatOptions?`: `NumberFormatOptions` How the number looks, in the user's locale: `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' }`, `{ style: 'percent' }`, `{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilogram' }`, `{ maximumFractionDigits: 2 }`…
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (shown in the error colour when `error` is `true`).
- `hideSteppers?`: `boolean` Hide the − / + buttons.
- `label?`: `string` Visible label. Use `aria-label` instead if there is no visible label.
- `max?`: `number`
- `min?`: `number`
- `name?`: `string` Form field name; submits the plain number (e.g. 100000, not "₹1,00,000").
- `onChange?`: `((value: number) => void)` Called with the parsed number (or NaN when cleared) as the value commits.
- `placeholder?`: `string`
- `readOnly?`: `boolean`
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.
- `startIcon?`: `ReactNode`
- `step?`: `number` Step for the buttons and arrow keys. Default 1.
- `value?`: `number | null` Controlled value; `null` when empty.

## Dropdown (`dropdown`)
Pick one value from a list.

```tsx
import { Dropdown } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add dropdown` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-dropdown--docs

### Dropdown
Dropdown: pick one value from a list. The chosen option's node lights up.
Built on the Popover and ListBox base components with React Aria:
typeahead on the closed and open list, arrow keys, Home/End, Escape,
groups with headings, screen-reader announcements, and a hidden native
select so plain forms and autofill work. `Select` is the same component.

Style hooks: `.sp-dropdown[data-open][data-invalid][data-disabled]`,
`__label`, `__trigger`, `__value[data-placeholder]`, `__chevron`,
`__helper`; the list uses `.sp-popover`, `.sp-listbox` and `.sp-list-item`.

- `options`: `(DropdownOption<V> | DropdownOptionGroup<V>)[]` Options, or groups of options with a heading: `{ label: 'Asia', options: [...] }`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "trigger" | "value" | "popover" | "option" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, trigger, value, popover, option, helper.
- `defaultValue?`: `string | number` Initial value when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when there are no options. Default "No options".
- `error?`: `ReactNode` An error message, or `true` to mark the field invalid and show `helperText` as the error.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (shown in the error colour when `error` is `true`).
- `label?`: `string` Visible label. Use `aria-label` instead if there is no visible label.
- `name?`: `string` Form field name; a hidden native select submits the value.
- `onBlur?`: `((event: FocusEvent<Element, Element>) => void)`
- `onChange?`: `((value: V) => void)` Called with the chosen option's value; its type follows the options (numbers stay numbers).
- `onFocus?`: `((event: FocusEvent<Element, Element>) => void)`
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)` Called when the list opens or closes.
- `placeholder?`: `string` Shown when nothing is selected. Default "Select an option".
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Height 36, 46 or 54px. Default `medium`.
- `startIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon at the start of the field.
- `value?`: `string | number | null` Controlled value (`null` for none).
- `appendIcon?`: `ReactNode` **Deprecated.** Put an `icon` on each option instead.
- `containerStyle?`: `CSSProperties` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames.root` or `className`.
- `forTeams?`: `boolean` **Deprecated.** Put `icon: <User />` on each option.
- `inputStyle?`: `CSSProperties` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames.trigger`.
- `itemStyle?`: `CSSProperties` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames.option`.
- `listContainerStyle?`: `CSSProperties` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames.popover`.
- `prependIcon?`: `ReactNode` **Deprecated.** Use `startIcon`.
- `showBorder?`: `boolean` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames` or CSS on `.sp-dropdown__trigger`.

## Combobox (`combobox`)
Type to search, then pick.

```tsx
import { Combobox } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add combobox` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-combobox--docs

### Combobox
Combobox: type to search a list, then pick. The field charges as you type
and the matching option lights up. Built on the InputBase, Popover and
ListBox base components with React Aria: filtering that ignores case and
accents, arrow keys, Enter to pick, Escape to close or clear, groups,
free entry, server-side search, and screen-reader announcements of
result counts.

Style hooks: `.sp-combobox[data-open][data-invalid][data-disabled][data-loading]`,
`__label`, `__helper`, `__spinner`; the field is `.sp-input-base`, the
list `.sp-popover`, `.sp-listbox` and `.sp-list-item`.

- `options`: `(ComboboxOption<V> | ComboboxOptionGroup<V>)[]` Options, or groups of options with a heading.
- `allowsCustomValue?`: `boolean` Keep typed text that matches no option (free entry, e.g. tags or a new city).
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"input" | "root" | "label" | "field" | "popover" | "option" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, field, input, popover, option, helper.
- `clearable?`: `boolean` Show a clear button when there is text. Default `true`.
- `defaultInputValue?`: `string` Initial text in the input when uncontrolled.
- `defaultValue?`: `string | number` Initial selected value when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when nothing matches. Default "No results".
- `error?`: `ReactNode` An error message, or `true` to mark the field invalid and show `helperText` as the error.
- `filter?`: `false | "contains" | "startsWith"` How options are matched to the typed text: `contains` (default), `startsWith`, or `false` when you filter yourself (e.g. server search). Matching ignores case and accents.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (shown in the error colour when `error` is `true`).
- `inputValue?`: `string` Controlled text in the input.
- `label?`: `string` Visible label. Use `aria-label` instead if there is no visible label.
- `loading?`: `boolean` Show a loading indicator, e.g. while fetching options.
- `loadingText?`: `ReactNode` Text shown in the list while `loading`. Default "Loading…".
- `menuTrigger?`: `"input" | "focus" | "manual"` When the list opens: on typing (`input`, default), on focus, or only with the button or arrow keys (`manual`).
- `name?`: `string` Form field name. Submits the selected value (or the typed text with `allowsCustomValue`).
- `onChange?`: `((value: V | null) => void)` Called with the chosen option's value, or `null` when cleared.
- `onInputChange?`: `((text: string) => void)` Called as the user types; use it to fetch options from a server (with `filter={false}`).
- `placeholder?`: `string` Placeholder text in the input.
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Height 36, 46 or 54px. Default `medium`.
- `startIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon at the start of the field, e.g. a search icon.
- `value?`: `string | number | null` Controlled selected value (`null` for none).

## DatePicker (`date-picker`)
DatePicker, DateRangePicker, Calendar and RangeCalendar: typed entry, presets, date rules, locales and calendar systems.

```tsx
import { DatePicker, DateRangePicker, Calendar, RangeCalendar } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add date-picker` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/inputs-datepicker--docs

### DatePicker
DatePicker: type a date or pick it from a calendar. The field lights up
while the calendar is open, and the picked day is a lit node with a spark.
Behaviour comes from React Aria: segment-by-segment typing in the
locale's order (DD/MM/YYYY in India, MM/DD/YYYY in the US), arrow keys to
adjust a segment, right-to-left layouts, other calendar systems, and a
dialog popover that restores focus.

Style hooks: `.sp-date-picker[data-open][data-invalid][data-disabled]`,
`__label`, `__control`, `.sp-date-field`, `__segment[data-placeholder]`,
`__trigger`, `__clear`, `__helper`, `__popover`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `calendar?`: `CalendarSystem` Calendar system to display, e.g. `indian` (Saka), `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`. Values stay JS Dates.
- `calendarClassNames?`: `Partial<Record<CalendarSlot, string>>` Extra classes for the calendar's parts (header, day, preset…).
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "control" | "field" | "trigger" | "popover" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, control, field, trigger, popover, helper.
- `clearable?`: `boolean` Show a clear button when a date is set. Default `true`.
- `defaultValue?`: `Date | null` Initial value when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `disabledDates?`: `Date[]` Days that can't be picked, e.g. holidays or booked days.
- `enabledDates?`: `Date[]` If set, only these days can be picked, e.g. open appointment slots.
- `error?`: `boolean` Marks the field invalid.
- `firstDayOfWeek?`: `"sun" | "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat"` First day of the week. Defaults to the locale's convention.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (or the error message when `error` is set).
- `isDateDisabled?`: `((date: Date) => boolean)` Return `true` for days that can't be picked, e.g. weekends. Combines with the lists above.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label above the field.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for names, digits and direction. Defaults to SparkProvider's or the browser's.
- `max?`: `Date` Latest selectable day.
- `min?`: `Date` Earliest selectable day.
- `name?`: `string` Name for a hidden input carrying the ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), for plain forms.
- `onChange?`: `((date: Date | null) => void)` Called with the picked or typed date, or `null` when cleared.
- `presets?`: `(DatePreset | DatePresetName)[]` Shortcut buttons under the calendar, replacing the Today button. Short names (`'today'`, `'tomorrow'`, `'+7d'`, `'+1m'`, `'-1y'`) or your own `{ label, value }` where value is a Date or a function returning one.
- `renderDay?`: `((date: Date, info: DayRenderInfo) => ReactNode)` Custom content for a day cell, e.g. a price or an event dot under the number.
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `showToday?`: `boolean` Show the Today button. Default `true` for Calendar, `false` for RangeCalendar. Ignored when `presets` is set.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.
- `todayLabel?`: `string` Label for the Today button, for other languages.
- `value?`: `Date | null` Controlled value; `null` for no date.
- `visibleMonths?`: `number` Months shown side by side. Default 1.
- `format?`: `DateTimeFormatOptions` **Deprecated.** The field now shows editable segments in the locale's order.
- `placeholder?`: `string` **Deprecated.** The field now shows editable segments in the locale's order.
- `weekStartsOn?`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` **Deprecated.** Use `firstDayOfWeek`. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

### DateRangePicker
DateRangePicker: type or pick a start and an end date; current flows
between them in the calendar. Two months side by side, shortcut buttons
(`presets`) under the calendar, and full control over which days can be
picked. Behaviour comes from React Aria: typed entry in the locale's order,
hover preview of the range, right-to-left, calendar systems.

Style hooks: `.sp-date-picker.sp-date-range-picker[data-open][data-invalid]`,
`__control`, `.sp-date-field`, `__dash`, `__trigger`, `__clear`, `__popover`.

- `allowsNonContiguousRanges?`: `boolean` Allow ranges that cross unavailable days. Default `false`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `calendar?`: `CalendarSystem` Calendar system to display, e.g. `indian` (Saka), `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`. Values stay JS Dates.
- `calendarClassNames?`: `Partial<Record<CalendarSlot, string>>` Extra classes for the calendar's parts.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "control" | "field" | "trigger" | "popover" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, control, field, trigger, popover, helper.
- `clearable?`: `boolean` Show a clear button when a range is set. Default `true`.
- `defaultValue?`: `DateRange | null` Initial range when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `disabledDates?`: `Date[]` Days that can't be picked, e.g. holidays or booked days.
- `enabledDates?`: `Date[]` If set, only these days can be picked, e.g. open appointment slots.
- `endName?`: `string` Hidden input with the end date (ISO), e.g. `checkOut`.
- `error?`: `boolean`
- `firstDayOfWeek?`: `"sun" | "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat"` First day of the week. Defaults to the locale's convention.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (or the error message when `error` is set).
- `isDateDisabled?`: `((date: Date) => boolean)` Return `true` for days that can't be picked, e.g. weekends. Combines with the lists above.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label above the field.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for names, digits and direction. Defaults to SparkProvider's or the browser's.
- `max?`: `Date` Latest selectable day.
- `min?`: `Date` Earliest selectable day.
- `name?`: `string` One hidden input with an ISO interval, e.g. `2026-12-01/2026-12-07`.
- `onChange?`: `((range: DateRange | null) => void)` Called with the picked or typed range, or `null` when cleared.
- `presets?`: `(RangePreset | RangePresetName)[]` Shortcut buttons under the calendar. Short names (`'+7d'` next 7 days, `'-30d'` last 30 days, `'thisWeek'`, `'thisMonth'`, `'thisYear'`, `'today'`) or your own `{ label, value }`.
- `renderDay?`: `((date: Date, info: DayRenderInfo) => ReactNode)` Custom content for a day cell, e.g. a price or an event dot under the number.
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.
- `startName?`: `string` Hidden input with the start date (ISO), e.g. `checkIn`.
- `value?`: `DateRange | null` Controlled range; `null` for none.
- `visibleMonths?`: `number` Months shown in the popover. Default 2.
- `weekStartsOn?`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` **Deprecated.** Use `firstDayOfWeek`. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

### Calendar
Calendar: a month grid. The selected day is a lit node, today is a ring,
and picking a day throws a spark. Shortcut buttons (`presets`) sit under
the grid. Behaviour comes from React Aria: arrows, Page Up/Down (Shift for
years), Home/End, right-to-left mirroring, localized names and digits,
other calendar systems, and announcements when the month changes.

Style hooks: `.sp-calendar`, `__header`, `__title`, `__nav`, `__months`,
`__grid`, `__weekday`, `__day` with `[data-selected]`, `[data-today]`,
`[data-unavailable]`, `[data-outside]`, `[data-focus-visible]`,
`__footer`, `__preset[data-active]`. Add classes with `classNames`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for the calendar.
- `autoFocus?`: `boolean` Move keyboard focus into the grid when the calendar mounts.
- `calendar?`: `CalendarSystem` Calendar system to display, e.g. `indian` (Saka), `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`. Values stay JS Dates.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<CalendarSlot, string>>` Extra classes for each part.
- `defaultValue?`: `Date | null` Initial selected day when uncontrolled.
- `disabledDates?`: `Date[]` Days that can't be picked, e.g. holidays or booked days.
- `enabledDates?`: `Date[]` If set, only these days can be picked, e.g. open appointment slots.
- `firstDayOfWeek?`: `"sun" | "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat"` First day of the week. Defaults to the locale's convention.
- `isDateDisabled?`: `((date: Date) => boolean)` Return `true` for days that can't be picked, e.g. weekends. Combines with the lists above.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for names, digits and direction. Defaults to SparkProvider's or the browser's.
- `max?`: `Date` Latest selectable day.
- `min?`: `Date` Earliest selectable day.
- `onChange?`: `((date: Date) => void)` Called with the picked day.
- `onEscape?`: `(() => void)` Called on Escape, so a custom popover can close.
- `presets?`: `(DatePreset | DatePresetName)[]` Shortcut buttons under the calendar, replacing the Today button. Short names (`'today'`, `'tomorrow'`, `'+7d'`, `'+1m'`, `'-1y'`) or your own `{ label, value }` where value is a Date or a function returning one.
- `renderDay?`: `((date: Date, info: DayRenderInfo) => ReactNode)` Custom content for a day cell, e.g. a price or an event dot under the number.
- `showToday?`: `boolean` Show the Today button. Default `true` for Calendar, `false` for RangeCalendar. Ignored when `presets` is set.
- `todayLabel?`: `string` Label for the Today button, for other languages.
- `value?`: `Date | null` The selected day.
- `visibleMonths?`: `number` Months shown side by side. Default 1.
- `weekStartsOn?`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` **Deprecated.** Use `firstDayOfWeek`. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

### RangeCalendar
RangeCalendar: pick a start and an end day; current flows between them.
Hovering after the first click previews the range. Shows two months with
`visibleMonths={2}`. Shortcut buttons (`presets`) sit under the grid.

Style hooks: as Calendar, plus `__day[data-range-start][data-range-end][data-in-range]`.

- `allowsNonContiguousRanges?`: `boolean` Allow ranges that cross unavailable days. Default `false`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for the calendar.
- `autoFocus?`: `boolean` Move keyboard focus into the grid when the calendar mounts.
- `calendar?`: `CalendarSystem` Calendar system to display, e.g. `indian` (Saka), `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`. Values stay JS Dates.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<CalendarSlot, string>>` Extra classes for each part.
- `defaultValue?`: `DateRange | null` Initial range when uncontrolled.
- `disabledDates?`: `Date[]` Days that can't be picked, e.g. holidays or booked days.
- `enabledDates?`: `Date[]` If set, only these days can be picked, e.g. open appointment slots.
- `firstDayOfWeek?`: `"sun" | "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat"` First day of the week. Defaults to the locale's convention.
- `isDateDisabled?`: `((date: Date) => boolean)` Return `true` for days that can't be picked, e.g. weekends. Combines with the lists above.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for names, digits and direction. Defaults to SparkProvider's or the browser's.
- `max?`: `Date` Latest selectable day.
- `min?`: `Date` Earliest selectable day.
- `onChange?`: `((range: DateRange) => void)` Called with the picked range once both ends are chosen.
- `onEscape?`: `(() => void)` Called on Escape, so a custom popover can close.
- `presets?`: `(RangePreset | RangePresetName)[]` Shortcut buttons under the calendar. Short names (`'+7d'` next 7 days, `'-30d'` last 30 days, `'thisWeek'`, `'thisMonth'`, `'thisYear'`, `'today'`) or your own `{ label, value }`.
- `renderDay?`: `((date: Date, info: DayRenderInfo) => ReactNode)` Custom content for a day cell, e.g. a price or an event dot under the number.
- `showToday?`: `boolean` Show the Today button. Default `true` for Calendar, `false` for RangeCalendar. Ignored when `presets` is set.
- `todayLabel?`: `string` Label for the Today button, for other languages.
- `value?`: `DateRange | null` The selected range.
- `visibleMonths?`: `number` Months shown side by side. Default 1.
- `weekStartsOn?`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` **Deprecated.** Use `firstDayOfWeek`. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

## DataTable (`data-table`)
Sort, search, filter, page and select rows; responsive div grid, no table library.

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add data-table` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/data-display-datatable--docs

### DataTable
DataTable: sort, search, filter, page and select rows. Built from divs on a
CSS grid (like MUI's Data Grid), so it adapts to its container: in narrow
spaces rows become labelled cards. The table logic is Spark UI's own
(`useDataTable`); React Aria supplies grid keyboard navigation and
screen-reader semantics. Sorted headers and selected rows light up.

Keyboard: arrows move between cells, Home/End and Page Up/Down jump,
Space selects a row, Enter activates it, Shift+click sorts by more than
one column.

Style hooks: `.sp-data-table[data-density][data-striped][data-responsive]`,
`__toolbar`, `__grid[aria-busy]`, `__header`, `__column[data-sorted][data-sortable]`,
`__row[data-selected][data-focus-visible]`, `__cell[data-align]`, `__footer`.

- `columns`: `DataTableColumn<RowT>[]`
- `data`: `RowT[]`
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name; describe what the table lists.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string`
- `bulkActions?`: `((rows: RowT[]) => ReactNode)` Actions shown when rows are selected, e.g. a delete button. Receives the selected rows.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "toolbar" | "grid" | "header" | "columnHeader" | "row" | "cell" | "footer", string>>` Extra classes for each part.
- `defaultFilters?`: `Record<string, unknown>`
- `defaultPage?`: `number`
- `defaultPageSize?`: `number`
- `defaultSearch?`: `string`
- `defaultSelectedKeys?`: `Iterable<string>`
- `defaultSort?`: `SortRule[]`
- `density?`: `"compact" | "normal" | "comfortable"` Row height. Default `normal`.
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when there are no rows. Default "No results".
- `filters?`: `Record<string, unknown>` Controlled per-column filter values, keyed by column.
- `getRowKey?`: `((row: RowT, index: number) => string)` Stable id for each row. Default: `row.id`, then the index.
- `loading?`: `boolean` Show placeholder rows while data loads.
- `manual?`: `boolean` Server-side mode: you sort, filter and page the data yourself (e.g. in an API call) and pass the current page as `data` with the total `rowCount`.
- `maxHeight?`: `string | number` Fix the height and scroll the body under a sticky header, e.g. `400`.
- `onFiltersChange?`: `((filters: Record<string, unknown>) => void)`
- `onPageChange?`: `((page: number) => void)`
- `onPageSizeChange?`: `((size: number) => void)`
- `onRowAction?`: `((row: RowT, key: string) => void)` Called when a row is activated (click, or Enter on the row).
- `onSearchChange?`: `((search: string) => void)`
- `onSelectionChange?`: `((keys: Set<string>) => void)`
- `onSortChange?`: `((sort: SortRule[]) => void)`
- `page?`: `number` Controlled page (0-based).
- `pageSize?`: `number` Rows per page; `0` turns paging off. Default 10.
- `pageSizeOptions?`: `number[]` Page sizes to offer. Default `[10, 25, 50]`. Pass `[]` to hide the picker.
- `responsive?`: `"stack" | "scroll"` In a narrow container: `stack` (default) turns rows into labelled cards; `scroll` keeps the grid and scrolls sideways.
- `rowCount?`: `number` Total rows on the server, for paging in `manual` mode.
- `search?`: `string` Controlled search text (matches any searchable column).
- `searchable?`: `boolean` Show a search box over the table.
- `searchPlaceholder?`: `string` Placeholder for the search box.
- `selectedKeys?`: `Set<string>` Controlled selected row keys.
- `selectionMode?`: `"none" | "single" | "multiple"` `multiple` adds checkboxes; `single` selects one row. Default `none`.
- `sort?`: `SortRule[]` Controlled sort rules (first wins).
- `stackBelow?`: `number` Container width (px) below which rows stack. Default 640.
- `striped?`: `boolean` Shade every other row.
- `toolbar?`: `ReactNode` Extra content in the toolbar, e.g. filter dropdowns or an export button.

## CommandPalette (`command-palette`)
A ⌘K launcher: search commands and pages, run with the keyboard.

```tsx
import { CommandPalette } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add command-palette` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/navigation-commandpalette--docs

### CommandPalette
CommandPalette: a ⌘K launcher. Type to find a command or page; arrows move
the lit node, Enter runs it, Escape closes. Focus stays in the search box
(ARIA combobox with an active option), the dialog traps focus and returns
it when closed. Groups, keywords, icons, shortcuts, links and async
results. Built on the Overlay and InputBase base components and the
shared list-item look.

Style hooks: `.sp-command`, `__panel`, `__input`, `__list`, `__group`,
`__heading`, `.sp-list-item[data-focused]`, `__empty`, `__footer`.

- `items`: `(Command | CommandGroup)[]` Commands, or groups of commands with a heading.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for the dialog. Default "Command palette".
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"panel" | "input" | "list" | "group" | "item" | "footer", string>>` Extra classes for each part: panel, input, list, group, item, footer.
- `closeOnSelect?`: `boolean` Close after a command runs. Default `true`.
- `defaultOpen?`: `boolean`
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when nothing matches. Default "No results".
- `filter?`: `boolean` Match commands to the search yourself. Default `true` (case- and accent-insensitive, best matches first).
- `hideFooter?`: `boolean` Hide the keyboard hints at the bottom.
- `hotkey?`: `string | false` Keyboard shortcut that opens and closes the palette. Default `mod+k` (⌘K on Mac, Ctrl+K elsewhere). `false` to turn off.
- `loading?`: `boolean` Show a loading line, e.g. while fetching.
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)`
- `onSearchChange?`: `((search: string) => void)` Called with the search text, e.g. to fetch results from a server (with `filter={false}`).
- `onSelect?`: `((command: Command) => void)` Called with the chosen command, after its own `onSelect`.
- `open?`: `boolean` Controlled open state.
- `placeholder?`: `string`

## Menu (`menu`)
Actions behind a button, with submenus.

```tsx
import { Menu } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add menu` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/navigation-menu--docs

### Menu
Menu: a list of actions behind a button (Edit, Duplicate, Delete). Not for
picking a value: use Dropdown for that. Built on the Popover base and the
shared list-item look, with React Aria's menu behaviour: arrow keys,
typeahead, Enter/Space to run, Escape to close, submenus that open with
the right arrow (left in right-to-left), sections, links, checkable items,
and focus returning to the trigger.

Style hooks: `.sp-menu`, `.sp-list-item[data-focused][data-danger][data-disabled][data-open]`,
`__end` (shortcut), `__chevron`, `__check`; trigger `.sp-menu-trigger`.

- `items`: `MenuEntry[]` Items, sections (`{ title, items }`) and submenus (`items` on an item).
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for the menu. Defaults to the trigger's text.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"trigger" | "popover" | "menu" | "item", string>>` Extra classes for each part: trigger, popover, menu, item.
- `closeOnSelect?`: `boolean` Close after an item is chosen. Default `true` (`false` by default with `multiple`).
- `defaultSelectedKeys?`: `Iterable<string>` Initial checked keys when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Text of the default trigger button. Ignored when `trigger` is set.
- `onAction?`: `((key: string) => void)` Called with the chosen item's key.
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)`
- `onSelectionChange?`: `((keys: Set<string>) => void)` Called with the checked keys.
- `placement?`: `"bottom start" | "bottom end" | "top start" | "top end"` Where the menu opens. Default `bottom start`.
- `selectedKeys?`: `Iterable<string>` Controlled checked keys.
- `selectionMode?`: `"none" | "single" | "multiple"` Make items checkable: `single` (like radio) or `multiple` (like checkboxes). Default `none`.
- `trigger?`: `ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>` Your own trigger, e.g. `<Button variant="text">` or an icon button. It must accept a ref.

## Sidebar (`sidebar`)
App navigation: sections, nested groups, collapsed rail, drawer on small screens.

```tsx
import { Sidebar } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add sidebar` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/navigation-sidebar--docs

### Sidebar
Sidebar: app navigation. Items sit on a wire down the side; the active
item is lit. Sections with headings, nested groups that open and close,
badges, links (with `aria-current="page"`), a collapsed icon-only rail
with tooltips, and a drawer on small screens. A real `<nav>` with lists,
so the browser's Tab order and screen-reader navigation just work.

Style hooks: `.sp-sidebar[data-collapsed]`, `__header`, `__nav`,
`__section`, `__heading`, `__item[data-active][data-open]`, `__badge`,
`__toggle`, `__footer`. Widths: `--sp-sidebar-width`, `--sp-sidebar-rail`.

- `items`: `(SidebarItem | SidebarSection)[]` Items, or sections of items with a heading.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name of the navigation. Default "Main".
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "header" | "nav" | "section" | "heading" | "item" | "footer" | "toggle", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, header, nav, section, heading, item, footer, toggle.
- `collapsed?`: `boolean` Icon-only rail (desktop). Controlled.
- `collapsible?`: `boolean` Show the collapse button. Default `true`.
- `defaultCollapsed?`: `boolean`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`
- `footer?`: `ReactNode | ((collapsed: boolean) => ReactNode)` Bottom area, e.g. the signed-in user.
- `header?`: `ReactNode | ((collapsed: boolean) => ReactNode)` Top area, e.g. a logo. Receives whether the sidebar is collapsed.
- `mobileBreakpoint?`: `number` Viewport width (px) below which the sidebar becomes a drawer. Default 768. `0` turns this off.
- `mobileOpen?`: `boolean` Drawer open state on small screens (controlled). Open it from your own menu button.
- `onChange?`: `((id: string) => void)`
- `onCollapsedChange?`: `((collapsed: boolean) => void)`
- `onMobileOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)`
- `value?`: `string` Active item id (controlled).

## Tabs (`tabs`)
Tabs on one wire; the active tab is lit.

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add tabs` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/navigation-tabs--docs

### Tabs
Tabs: every tab sits on one wire. The active tab is the lit segment, and the
current slides along the wire when you switch. Behaviour comes from React
Aria: arrow keys (mirrored in right-to-left languages), Home/End, vertical
orientation, and automatic or manual activation.

Works when rendered from a React Server Component: tabs register
themselves instead of being read out of `children`.

Style hooks: `.sp-tabs[data-orientation]`, `.sp-tab-list`,
`.sp-tab[aria-selected][data-focus-visible]`, `.sp-tab-list__current`, `.sp-tab-panel`.

- `children`: `ReactNode` A TabList and its TabPanels.
- `activation?`: `"automatic" | "manual"` `automatic` (default): arrow keys select as they move. `manual`: arrow keys move focus; Enter or Space selects (use for slow panels).
- `className?`: `string`
- `color?`: `Tone` Colour of the lit segment. Default `brand`.
- `defaultValue?`: `string` Initially active tab when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first enabled tab.
- `onChange?`: `((value: string) => void)` Called with the newly selected tab's value.
- `orientation?`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"` Lay tabs out in a row (default) or a column. Arrow keys follow.
- `value?`: `string` Controlled active tab.

### TabList


- `children`: `ReactNode` <Tab> elements.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Describe the set of tabs for screen readers.
- `className?`: `string`

### Tab
One tab. Use inside <TabList>.

- `value`: `string` Matches a TabPanel's `value`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` (default `false`)
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` Icon shown before the label.

### TabPanel


- `value`: `string` Matches a Tab's `value`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.

## Accordion (`accordion`)
Sections that power on as they open.

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add accordion` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/navigation-accordion--docs

### Accordion
Accordion: a stack of circuits. Opening a section closes its circuit: the
wire beside it lights up and current runs down it.

Style hooks: `.sp-accordion`, `__item[data-state="open"|"closed"]`, `__wire`,
`__trigger`, `__chevron`, `__panel`.

- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultOpen?`: `string[]` Sections open at first, by `value`.
- `multiple?`: `boolean` Allow several sections open at once. Default `false`.

### AccordionItem


- `title`: `ReactNode` Text of the header button.
- `value`: `string` Unique key for this section.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`

## Modal (`modal`)
A dialog that powers on, with focus trapping.

```tsx
import { Modal } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add modal` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/overlays-modal--docs

### Modal
Modal: a power cut. The page dims with a flicker and the dialog is the only
thing left lit. Behaviour comes from React Aria: focus is contained and
restored, the page behind is hidden from screen readers and can't scroll,
and Escape or an outside click closes it. Built on the Overlay base.

Style hooks: `.sp-modal`, `__backdrop`, `__panel[data-size]`, `__current`,
`__header`, `__title`, `__description`, `__close`, `__body`, `__actions`.

- `onClose`: `() => void` Called on Escape, the close button, or a click outside the dialog.
- `open`: `boolean` Whether the dialog is shown.
- `title`: `ReactNode` Dialog heading; also its accessible name.
- `actions?`: `ReactNode` Buttons, usually. Rendered right-aligned in the footer.
- `className?`: `string` Class for the dialog panel.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "backdrop" | "panel" | "header" | "title" | "description" | "close" | "body" | "actions", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, backdrop, panel, header, title, description, close, body, actions.
- `closeOnBackdrop?`: `boolean` Close when the user clicks outside the dialog. Default `true`.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` Supporting text under the title; read as the dialog's description.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Max width: small 400px, medium 520px, large 720px.

## Drawer (`drawer`)
A panel that slides in from an edge, with focus trapping.

```tsx
import { Drawer } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add drawer` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/overlays-drawer--docs

### Drawer
Drawer: a panel that slides in from an edge, for filters, details, forms
or navigation on small screens. Current runs along its inner edge as it
powers on. Built on the Overlay base: focus is trapped and returned,
the page behind is hidden from screen readers and doesn't scroll, and
Escape or a backdrop click closes it.

Style hooks: `.sp-drawer[data-placement]`, `__backdrop`, `__panel`,
`__header`, `__title`, `__description`, `__body`, `__actions`, `__close`.
Variable: `--sp-drawer-size`.

- `onClose`: `() => void` Called on Escape, the close button or (when `dismissable`) a click on the backdrop.
- `open`: `boolean` Whether the drawer is open.
- `actions?`: `ReactNode` Footer content, e.g. Cancel and Save buttons.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible title.
- `className?`: `string`
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "backdrop" | "panel" | "header" | "title" | "description" | "body" | "actions" | "close", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, backdrop, panel, header, title, description, body, actions, close.
- `closeButton?`: `boolean` Show the × button. Default `true`.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` Text under the title.
- `dismissable?`: `boolean` Close on a click on the backdrop. Default `true`.
- `placement?`: `"start" | "end" | "top" | "bottom"` Edge it slides from. `start`/`end` follow reading direction (`end` is the right in English, the left in Arabic). Default `end`.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large" | "full" | (string & {})` `small` (20rem), `medium` (28rem, default), `large` (40rem), `full`, or any CSS length.
- `title?`: `ReactNode` Heading; also the dialog's accessible name.

## Tooltip (`tooltip`)
A hint that flickers on.

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add tooltip` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/overlays-tooltip--docs

### Tooltip
Tooltip: a short charged label that arcs out from its trigger on hover or
keyboard focus. Behaviour comes from React Aria: hover delay with warm-up
across nearby tooltips, instant on keyboard focus, Escape dismisses.

Style hooks: `.sp-tooltip` (wrapper), `.sp-tooltip__bubble[data-placement]`.

- `children`: `ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>` A single focusable element, e.g. a Button.
- `title`: `ReactNode` Tooltip text. Keep it short; it is read as the trigger's description.
- `className?`: `string` Class for the tooltip bubble.
- `delay?`: `number` Delay before showing on hover, in ms. Default 250. Keyboard focus shows it at once.
- `placement?`: `"top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right"` Side of the trigger to show on. Default `top`.

## Toast (`toast`)
Notifications.

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add toast` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/feedback-toast--docs

### ToastProvider
Wrap your app once. Toasts stack bottom-right (max 5); the bottom bar
discharges as the timer runs and pauses on hover or focus.

Style hooks: `.sp-toast-region`, `.sp-toast[data-tone]`, `__led`, `__title`,
`__description`, `__action`, `__close`, `__timer`.

No props.

### ToastShowOptions
Options for `toast.show()`. Wrap your app in `<ToastProvider>`, then
`const toast = useToast(); toast.show({ title: 'Saved', tone: 'success' })`.

- `title`: `ReactNode` Bold first line.
- `action?`: `{ label: string; onClick: () => void; }` One action button, e.g. Undo. The toast closes after it runs.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` Optional second line.
- `duration?`: `number` Auto-dismiss after this many ms. `0` keeps it until closed. Default 4000.
- `tone?`: `Tone` Default `brand`. `error` toasts are announced immediately (role="alert").

## Card (`card`)
Card, CardHeader, CardFooter and Skeleton.

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, Skeleton } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add card` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/data-display-card--docs

### Card
Card: a raised panel. `live` cards carry current; `interactive` cards glow on hover.
Style hooks: `.sp-card[data-live][data-interactive][data-padding]`, `__current`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `as?`: `"div" | "article" | "section" | "li"` Render as another element, e.g. `article` or `section`.
- `interactive?`: `boolean` Hover lift and glow, for clickable cards. Put the link or button inside.
- `live?`: `boolean` A live card has current running along its top edge.
- `padding?`: `"none" | "small" | "medium" | "large"` Inner spacing. Default `medium`.

### CardHeader


- `title`: `ReactNode`
- `action?`: `ReactNode` Shown on the right, e.g. a Badge or menu button.
- `media?`: `ReactNode` Shown on the left, e.g. an Avatar or icon.
- `subtitle?`: `ReactNode`

### Skeleton
Skeleton: a placeholder that shimmers like a line charging up.

- `height?`: `string | number` Number (px) or any CSS length.
- `lines?`: `number` (default `1`) For `text`: number of lines. The last line is shorter.
- `shape?`: `"text" | "rect" | "circle"` (default `rect`) `circle` for avatars, `text` for lines of copy.
- `width?`: `string | number` Number (px) or any CSS length. Defaults to 100%.

## Avatar (`avatar`)
Avatar and AvatarGroup.

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add avatar` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/data-display-avatar--docs

### Avatar
Avatar: a photo or initials, with an optional status LED. An online user's
LED pulses with current.
Style hooks: `.sp-avatar[data-size][data-status]`, `__face`, `__led`.

- `name`: `string` Full name: used for initials and the accessible label.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large" | "xlarge"` Default `medium` (40px).
- `src?`: `string` Photo URL. Falls back to initials if missing or broken.
- `status?`: `AvatarStatus` Status LED. `online` pulses.

### AvatarGroup
AvatarGroup: overlapping avatars wired together, with a "+N" overflow.

- `people`: `AvatarProps[]`
- `max?`: `number` (default `4`) Show at most this many; the rest become a "+N" chip. Default 4.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large" | "xlarge"` (default `medium`)

## Indicators (`indicators`)
Badge, Progress and Spinner.

```tsx
import { Badge, Progress, Spinner } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add indicators` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/feedback-badge--docs

### Badge
Badge: a status label with an LED. Pulsing means "live". Style hooks: `.sp-badge`, `__led`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "led", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, led.
- `led?`: `boolean` Show the status LED. Default `true`.
- `pulse?`: `boolean` Pulse the LED: something is live or in progress.
- `tone?`: `Tone | "neutral"` Default `brand`.
- `variant?`: `"soft" | "solid"` `soft` tinted background (default) or `solid` fill.

### Progress
Progress: a charge bar. At 100% the bar is fully charged and current flows.
Style hooks: `.sp-progress[data-state="charging"|"charged"|"indeterminate"]`, `__track`, `__fill`.

- `label?`: `ReactNode` Text above the bar; also its accessible name when a string.
- `showValue?`: `boolean` Show the percentage next to the label. Default `true` when determinate.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Bar thickness: 4, 8 or 12px. Default `medium`.
- `tone?`: `Tone` Default `brand`.
- `value?`: `number` 0–100. Leave undefined for an indeterminate bar.

### Spinner
Spinner: an arc of current with a spark at its head. Style hooks: `.sp-spinner`, `__track`, `__arc`, `__head`.

- `label?`: `string` Accessible label. Default "Loading".
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` 16, 24 or 36px. Default `medium`.
- `tone?`: `Tone` Default `brand`.

## SparkProvider (`provider`)
App-wide default props, slot classes and locale.

```tsx
import { SparkProvider } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add provider` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/foundations-customization--docs

### SparkProvider
SparkProvider: set app-wide defaults and slot class names once, the way
MUI's `theme.components` works. Nested providers merge with their parent.
Styling still comes from `styles.css`; this provider only changes props.

- `components?`: `SparkComponentsConfig` Defaults for every instance of a component, e.g. `{ Button: { defaultProps: { variant: 'outlined' } }, Switch: { classNames: { bulb: 'my-bulb' } } }`. Props set on an instance always win.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for dates, number formats and keyboard direction, e.g. `hi-IN`, `ar-EG`, `en-US`. Right-to-left locales mirror arrow keys. Defaults to the parent provider's, then the browser's.

## Base components (`base`)
ButtonBase, InputBase, Popover, ListBox and Overlay: the building blocks under the other components.

```tsx
import { ButtonBase, InputBase, Popover, ListItemContent, ListBox, Overlay } from '@sparkwire/core/base';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add base` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/?path=/docs/foundations-base-components--docs

### ButtonBase
ButtonBase: the pressable foundation under Button, IconButton and menu
triggers. Handles disabled state for any element, `type="button"` by
default, and the spark burst. No visual style of its own beyond
`.sp-button-base`; build your own buttons on it.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `as?`: `ElementType` Render as another element or component, e.g. `"a"` or a router Link.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` (default `false`) Dead circuit: no clicks, no sparks. Uses `disabled` on buttons, `aria-disabled` otherwise.
- `href?`: `string` Link target when rendered as an anchor.
- `spark?`: `boolean` (default `true`) Throw sparks from the press point on click. Default `true`.
- `sparkColors?`: `string[]` Spark colours. Default: the theme's spark colours.

### InputBase
InputBase: the field shell under Textfield and Combobox. One bordered box
holds the input and its adornments, lights up on focus, dashes when
disabled, and focuses the input when you click anywhere in it. Build your
own fields on it; label and help text are up to you (see Field).

Style hooks: `.sp-input-base[data-variant][data-size][data-invalid][data-disabled]`,
`__input`, `__adornment`. Focus uses `:focus-within`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element. @see aria-labelledby.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. @see aria-describedby.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"input" | "root" | "adornment", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, input, adornment.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` (default `false`)
- `endAdornment?`: `ReactNode` Shown after the input, e.g. a clear button or a chevron.
- `error?`: `boolean` (default `false`) Marks the field invalid.
- `rootProps?`: `(HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { [key: `data-${string}`]: unknown; })` Props for the outer shell (data attributes, handlers, style).
- `rootRef?`: `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` Ref for the outer shell, e.g. to anchor a popover.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` (default `medium`) Height 36, 46 or 54px. Default `medium`.
- `startAdornment?`: `ReactNode` Shown before the input, e.g. an icon or a currency sign.
- `variant?`: `"outlined" | "filled" | "standard"` (default `outlined`) `outlined` (default), `filled` or `standard` (underline only).

### Popover
Popover: a floating panel attached to a trigger, under Dropdown, Combobox,
Menu and DatePicker. Positions itself and flips to stay on screen, renders
in a portal that keeps the current theme, closes on outside click and
Escape, and has hidden dismiss buttons for screen readers.

Style hooks: `.sp-popover[data-placement]`.

- `state`: `OverlayTriggerState` Open state, from `useOverlayTriggerState` or a component state (select, combobox, menu).
- `triggerRef`: `RefObject<Element | null>` The element the popover is attached to. Its theme is copied to the popover.
- `className?`: `string`
- `disableFocusManagement?`: `boolean` Leave focus handling to the content (used by submenus).
- `matchTriggerWidth?`: `boolean` Make the popover at least as wide as the trigger.
- `style?`: `CSSProperties`

### ListItemContent
The inside of a list row: icon, label, description and an end slot. Shared by options and menu items.

- `label`: `ReactNode`
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `end?`: `ReactNode` Shown at the end, e.g. a keyboard shortcut.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode`

### ListBox
ListBox: a list of options to choose from, under Dropdown and Combobox.
Each option is a node on a wire: the selected one lights up. Supports
groups with headings, icons, descriptions, disabled options and
screen-reader announcements.

Style hooks: `.sp-listbox`, `.sp-list-section`, `__heading`,
`.sp-list-item[data-focused][data-selected][data-disabled]`, `__icon`,
`__label`, `__description`, `__check`, `.sp-listbox__empty`.

- `state`: `ListState<T>` List state from `useListState`, `useSelectState` or `useComboBoxState`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
- `className?`: `string`
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when there are no options.
- `listBoxRef?`: `Ref<HTMLUListElement>`
- `optionClassName?`: `string` Extra class for every option row.
- `optionStyle?`: `CSSProperties` Inline style for every option row.

### Overlay
Overlay: the full-screen layer under Modal (and future Drawer and
Sheet). Renders in a portal that keeps the current theme, dims the page,
traps and restores focus, hides the page from screen readers, blocks
scrolling, and closes on Escape or an outside click.

Style hooks: `.sp-overlay`, `.sp-overlay__backdrop`.

- `children`: `(panel: { panelProps: HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>; panelRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement>; }) => ReactNode` Render the panel. Spread `panelProps` on it and attach `panelRef`. Use a component here if you need hooks (e.g. `useDialog`).
- `onClose`: `() => void` Called on Escape or (when `dismissable`) a click outside the panel.
- `open`: `boolean` Whether the overlay is shown.
- `backdropClassName?`: `string` Class for the dimmed backdrop.
- `className?`: `string` Class for the full-screen root.
- `dismissable?`: `boolean` Close on a click outside the panel. Default `true`.
- `keyboardDismissDisabled?`: `boolean` Ignore Escape. Default `false`.
